title: 3.1 POLLUTION
summary: Combustion releases pollutants both as trapped impurities and as unavoidable byproducts of the oxidation reaction itself, and this chapter surveys the main categories: particulate matter, heavy metals like mercury, sulfur and nitrogen oxides, and the two carbon oxides. It distinguishes carbon dioxide, an unavoidable climatic concern tied to fuel chemistry, from carbon monoxide, a toxic but engineerable byproduct, and traces how sulfur and nitrogen oxides form and contribute to acid rain. These pollutants operate at different geographic scales, from local to global, and the chapter closes with the general strategies available for managing toxic emissions — neutralizing, diluting, or otherwise controlling them.
